verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: Each commit must let a reviewer understand the problem, the solution, every changed file, the evidence that it works, important tradeoffs, and remaining work without reconstructing a chat. Detailed explanations supplement the diff; they must not contradict it or replace code review.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: The project policy is **no commit with a failed, blocked, missing, stale, or skipped required check**. This is stronger than merely requiring green checks before merging. Local hooks can be bypassed by Git options or configuration; they are useful controls, not an absolute security boundary. Remote CI and protected branches provide a second enforcement layer once hosting exists. Their existence alone does not validate local commits before creation. [Git hooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks), [GitHub branch protection](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches).

rule: - Commit one coherent, complete purpose at a time. Keep supporting tests, docs, migrations, and dependency changes with the behavior they support. Split unrelated cleanup or features into independently valid commits.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Explain the concrete before/after behavior and why it matters. Describe mechanisms and tradeoffs precisely; avoid vague statements such as "improve code," "various fixes," or "production-ready."

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Write direct, natural engineering prose. No mentions of AI, models, assistants, prompting, generated-by signatures, or tool-credit boilerplate in commit messages. Do not invent a human author, reviewer, sign-off, or test execution. Preserve legally required attribution in source and truthful Git identity.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - No email address is required in the commit subject, body, or trailers. Keep personal email addresses out of commit messages. Git author/committer metadata is separate: use the authorized public author name and a GitHub-provided noreply address, configured per repository, to avoid publishing a personal address. Do not invent attribution or sign-off trailers.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Keep the subject short enough to scan; target 50–72 characters and use imperative wording. Wrap body prose around 80–100 columns when practical. Keep paths, URLs, commands, and file-ledger rows intact even when longer.

rule: - Depth means useful evidence and reasoning, not repeated claims. Every section below is required; `None — <reason>` or `N/A — <reason>` is acceptable where true. Do not invent decisions or downloads to fill space.

rule: - Use Git's added/deleted line counts from the final staged diff. Here `LOC` means changed text lines as Git reports them, including comments/blank lines/docs; it is not a language-aware code metric or a measure of productivity.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Report additions and deletions separately, even for edited files. Always use `+A -D LOC`. Also report net `A-D` and overall totals. Never present the net alone as the amount of work.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - For pure renames, report `+0 -0 LOC` if that is the diff result; do not count the entire file as newly authored. Record the rename detection mode so counts can be reproduced. For copies, identify origin and do not imply original authorship.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Binary files have `LOC: N/A (binary)`; record old/new byte size and purpose when available. Git's `- -` numstat values are not zeros. For LFS objects identify the object/size; pointer text counts are not asset size. For submodules record old/new commit IDs; do not label a gitlink line as implementation LOC. For mode-only changes record old/new modes and `+0 -0 LOC`.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Include lockfile/generated text in totals but identify their subtotal separately from hand-maintained source/tests/docs. Totals must reconcile with the file rows; list non-text changes separately.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Generate factual counts mechanically; write the explanation after reviewing the actual diff. Do not estimate counts or count unstaged/untracked files outside the proposed commit.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: For automation, use `-z` on name-status/numstat, parse NUL-delimited records including the special rename layout, and preserve Unicode/spaces in paths. Never split paths on whitespace. Record diff settings including rename detection and algorithm; normalize the future ledger tool to `--diff-algorithm=myers` for both generation and validation. These counts reflect the chosen diff, not an intrinsic property of a file. [Git diff documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff).

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: For an amend, compare the final candidate tree against the original commit's first parent, not against the commit being amended; regenerate the **entire replacement message**, not only the new delta. An amended root commit uses the empty tree. For a merge commit, declare first-parent comparison and distinguish incoming changes from conflict resolutions; retain other parent IDs in evidence. A squash commit gets a fresh ledger against its actual target parent. Do not concatenate obsolete messages/counts. After rebase/cherry-pick/conflict resolution, regenerate evidence for the new candidate tree and parent.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: A commit is allowed only when the exact proposed contents pass the complete registered commit gate. Existing failures still block; being unrelated to the task does not turn a red build green. Failed/flaky tests must be investigated and fixed; repeated reruns until green are not a substitute. Missing tools/devices/credentials or unavailable runners are `BLOCKED`, not `PASS`.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: Once an app exists, documentation-only commits still run the required app build/test gate under this policy. They do not need artificial new unit tests for prose. Before any executable app exists, a genuinely documentation/asset-only initial snapshot may record app build/tests as `N/A — no executable app exists`, with real documentation/asset validation. This exception ends with application scaffolding; an app with no configured tests/build commands is blocked, not exempt.

Use a trusted pre-commit runner that can validate the same candidate tree before commit creation; otherwise wait until such validation is available. Do not claim a Windows check validates an iOS build. Ordinary CI triggered only after committing cannot satisfy this pre-commit requirement retroactively.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Stage only when authorized. Identify the staged tree and intended parent/base. `git write-tree` writes a tree object representing the index; it does not create a commit. Capture its full object ID for validation evidence. [Git write-tree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-write-tree).

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Validate in a clean isolated checkout/export of that tree, or prove the validation workspace matches it and contains no untracked/ignored inputs that affect the result. Do not rely only on `git status`; ignored files and local dependencies can change outcomes. Recreate dependencies from the declared inputs.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Handle partial staging correctly: an unstaged fix must not make a broken staged file pass. Do not automatically stash, overwrite, or stage unrelated work to work around this problem. An isolated candidate workspace is preferable when the user's tree is dirty.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Record tree ID, base/parent ID, tool versions, OS/architecture, relevant sanitized configuration, dependency/lockfile identity, commands/results, timestamp/time zone, and report/run references. Store bulky logs outside committed source with appropriate retention/access.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Recheck tree ID and parent immediately before committing. Any change to code, tests, config, lockfiles, generated content, or other staged files invalidates the earlier full gate evidence; rerun for the new snapshot. Parent changes also require renewed evidence. A message-only edit needs message validation again but does not alter the tree.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Do not place a report containing its own final tree ID inside that tree: this creates a self-reference. Keep the gate report external and place its identifier/tree ID in the commit message. A commit's own hash cannot be known in advance; do not invent one. Attach later CI links to the PR/status rather than amending history merely to insert them.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Do not change the staged snapshot in hooks. If formatters fix files, stop, review/restage deliberately, and rerun the gate. Optimize with safe build caches keyed to inputs, not by reusing stale verdicts.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - A tracked `pre-commit` hook runs or verifies the complete gate for the final candidate and fails closed. A tracked `commit-msg` hook validates the subject, required sections, absence of placeholders, all paths/actions/counts/totals, and matching gate evidence. Message text saying `PASS` is never evidence by itself.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Use one canonical gate implementation from local hooks and CI. Install hooks explicitly per clone/worktree and document activation. Inspect existing `core.hooksPath`, hooks, and tooling before configuring; integrate rather than replacing somebody's existing hooks.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Add automated checks that a broken build, failing test, missing command, zero-test suite, wrong file count, stale tree evidence, and unstaged-fix/partial-staging case each prevent a commit. Also prove a valid candidate commits successfully in an isolated test repository. Test merge/amend workflows if supported.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Policy forbids `--no-verify`, disabling hooks/checks, environment skip switches, lower-level commit creation, or alternate workflows to evade validation. New clones and GUI clients must be checked for hook activation. Do not claim local controls are tamper-proof.

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Require trusted CI checks and reviewed changes on protected shared branches once hosting exists. Validate the latest candidate and integration with the target branch; block stale results and bypass paths. Do not accept a skipped/neutral wrapper job as proof that required builds/tests ran. Configure platform-specific jobs explicitly. [Required status checks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

verification: Run staged gate and commit-msg checks; reconcile Git ledger and review rationale, risks and exclusions.
rule: - Account for squash/merge automation: it must preserve/rebuild the complete message and validate the final tree; a default one-line squash message is insufficient. If strict pre-creation validation cannot be provided by a hosted merge flow, use a compatible validated workflow rather than silently weakening this rule.

For a prepared multiline message, save the exact text to a temporary UTF-8 file and use `git commit --file <message-file>` only after authorization and gate success. Do not interpolate multiline prose into a shell command. [Git commit documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit).
